- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) — model tends to be too bullish.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment <0.3) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) — model overcorrects or fails to adjust downward.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, especially if sentiment is low.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model reacts to sentiment shifts with 2–3 day delay — adjust forecasts by adding 0.1–0.3 to forecast if sentiment rises sharply.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate upward momentum in late horizon (days 20–30) — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast if sentiment is rising and price is trending up.
- Avoid “flat” forecasts when sentiment is volatile — model tends to ignore sentiment swings in low-variance periods.
